name: Cheque dishonour complaint (NI Act s.138)
status: DRAFT - written from general knowledge; every rule must be validated by a practising advocate before real use

inputs.name: bank_information_received_date
inputs.label: Date the complainant received the bank's dishonour information

inputs.name: notice_received_date
inputs.label: Date the drawer received the demand notice

deadline_rules.label: Last day to present the cheque (3 months; also check the cheque's own validity)
Last day to send the demand notice (30 days from the bank's information)
Last day to file the complaint (one month after cause of action; delay can be condoned for sufficient cause)

deadline_note: Day-counting convention and court holidays are NOT applied. The advocate must confirm every date before relying on it.

stages.name: Cheque dishonoured
actions: Collect the cheque, bank return memo, agreement and ledger
Confirm the cheque was presented within its validity period
Record the date the bank's information was received

stages.name: Demand notice
actions: Send the legal notice by trackable means within 30 days of the bank's information
Keep the postal receipt and tracking proof
Record the date the drawer received the notice

stages.name: Waiting period for payment
actions: Track delivery proof of the notice
Diarise the end of the 15-day payment period
Prepare the complaint documents in advance

stages.name: Complaint filed
actions: File the complaint with affidavit and documents within one month after the payment period ends
Prepare the list of documents and witnesses

stages.name: Cognizance and summons
actions: Make sure summons is served on the accused
Track the date fixed for the accused's appearance

stages.name: Accused appears
actions: Check the bail conditions
Consider an application for interim compensation (s.143A)
Supply copies of documents to the accused

stages.name: Plea and complainant's evidence
actions: File the evidence affidavit (s.145) with original documents
Prepare for cross-examination
Mark and exhibit the documents

stages.name: Accused's statement and defence
actions: Review the accused's statement and defence
Prepare the rebuttal and questions for defence witnesses

stages.name: Final arguments
actions: Prepare written arguments with verified citations
Prepare a chronology and list of exhibits

stages.name: Judgment, compounding or appeal
actions: Read the judgment and note the appeal and compliance periods
Consider appeal, execution or compounding papers (s.147, s.148)
Tell the client the outcome and next steps

routes.name: Demand notice, then criminal complaint under s.138
routes.summary: The statutory route: send the demand notice in time, wait out the 15-day payment period, then file the complaint within one month of the cause of action.
steps: Present the cheque within its validity (three months) and keep the bank's return memo
Send the written demand notice within 30 days of the bank's information
Wait for the drawer's 15-day payment period after the notice is received
If unpaid, file the complaint within one month of the cause of action
consider: Interim compensation of up to 20% of the cheque amount can be sought (s.143A)
The offence carries imprisonment up to two years, a fine up to twice the cheque amount, or both (s.138)
Where the drawer is a company, the persons in charge can be joined (s.141)
risks: A notice sent after the 30-day window defeats the complaint
Delay in filing can be condoned only for sufficient cause (s.142(1)(b))

routes.name: Settlement by payment during the notice period
routes.summary: The demand notice itself is the lever: if the drawer pays within 15 days of receiving it, the cause of action does not arise. Keep the complaint dates alive in case the payment does not come.
steps: Send the demand notice in time and record how and when it was received
Record any part payment or settlement offer in writing
Do not let the complaint deadline pass while talks continue
consider: Once a complaint is pending, the offence can still be compounded (s.147)
Get any settlement terms signed by the client before they are communicated
risks: Talks do not extend the statutory periods

routes.name: Civil recovery suit alongside or instead of the criminal complaint
routes.summary: A suit for recovery on the cheque or the underlying debt (for example a summary suit under Order XXXVII CPC) can be pursued alongside the complaint. The playbook has no fixed-rule deadline for this route.
steps: Check the limitation period for the suit separately
Decide whether the cheque or the underlying transaction is the cause of action
Confirm the court's pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction
consider: Civil and criminal proceedings can run together
Court fee is payable on the claim
risks: Limitation for the suit is not computed by this product. Check it before relying on this route
routes.authority: CPC Order XXXVII (verify applicability to the instrument)
